message: Persistent anxiety and stress about gardening yields (especially tomatoes); it intensified a few months ago when I noticed the tomatoes growing slower than usual; every time I check on or think about the garden I worry the whole season's harvest will fail.

After an unexpected car tire replacement increased my expenses, I worry I cannot save enough for a class trip to Japan; I persistently feel stress, anxiety, and despair, which intensifies as the trip approaches; anxiety and hopelessness recur whenever I think about the trip or finances, especially after unexpected expenses.

Because I did not receive a raise, I feel like a terrible employee at work.
After a recent divorce, I feel I have been a failure my whole life; these feelings of failure occur almost daily and have made me lose enjoyment in gardening, which I once loved.

I often feel people are negatively judging my work, especially when I paint portraits for others. This feeling began a few months ago when my girlfriend smiled while I was painting her portrait.
I worry people will not like me because of my tattoos (specifically six cat tattoos); this belief causes anxiety and social withdrawal.

I don't want to work, because I feel it is a form of control, and I will always struggle financially and produce nothing. These thoughts began in my early twenties and gradually worsened after difficulties finding work and pressure from family to be independent; I lack motivation to look for work, and the thoughts appear daily, especially when my parents mention job hunting. I try to distract myself with video games, but the thoughts persist.
I feel people think I am smart only because I read a lot of books, and anyone could read like me, which makes me feel not truly appreciated and lacking recognition.

Because I accumulated heavy debt as a graduate student, I feel despair and helplessness; this worry about financial security has continued to worsen since graduate school, affecting my sleep, eating, academic performance, and relationships.
